title: DeepMind started by teaching an AI Atari games
summary: DeepMind was founded in 2010 by three founders and first taught an AI to play Atari games by trial and error. Google confirmed it would acquire the company on January 26, 2014, and in March 2016 DeepMind's AlphaGo beat a Go professional 4 to 1.

beats.say: A startup's AI learned Atari games by trial and error.
beats.cap: An AI learned Atari by trial and error

beats.say: DeepMind was founded in two thousand ten by three founders.
Its goal was a general purpose AI, useful for almost anything.
Early on, its AI played Atari games like Breakout, Pong and Space Invaders.
It was given no programmed knowledge of how to play.
On January twenty sixth, twenty fourteen, Google confirmed it was acquiring DeepMind.
Reports put the price between four hundred and six hundred fifty million dollars.
In March twenty sixteen, DeepMind's AlphaGo beat a professional Go player, four games to one.
That match came about two years after the Google deal.
The same company went from Atari games to a Go match.

claims.note: Christian Science Monitor: Google confirmed the acquisition on Sunday, January 26, 2014; Wikipedia: 26 January 2014
Christian Science Monitor: Re/Code first reported the deal at $400 million
Wikipedia: the reported price ranged from $400 million to $650 million

facts.claim: DeepMind was founded in November 2010 by Demis Hassabis, Shane Legg and Mustafa Suleyman, aiming at general-purpose AI
facts.note: Wikipedia: founded November 2010 by Hassabis, Legg and Suleyman; goal a general-purpose AI 'useful and effective for almost anything'

facts.claim: DeepMind first taught an AI to play Atari games such as Breakout, Pong and Space Invaders, with no programmed knowledge, by trial and error
facts.note: Wikipedia: first taught AI to play 1970s and 1980s Atari games, including Breakout, Pong and Space Invaders; no programmed knowledge of how to play; learned through trial and error

facts.claim: Google confirmed the DeepMind acquisition on January 26, 2014; the price was reported at $400 million to $650 million
facts.note: Christian Science Monitor: confirmed Sunday January 26, 2014, Re/Code reported $400 million; Wikipedia: reported price ranged from $400 million to $650 million

facts.claim: In March 2016 AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol, a 9-dan professional, four games to one in a five-game match
facts.note: Wikipedia: March 2016, AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol 4-1 in a five-game match
